values.DataCenterNotes: A January 2026 Rextag industry blog names data centers, with utilities, industry and coal retirements, as demand drivers for gas pipeline expansion in Wisconsin, and names the Wisconsin Reliability Project as one of the expansions meeting that demand. It says Microsoft and Meta, among others, are looking at Wisconsin and Illinois for data center sites. No specific data center is tied to this pipeline.

verifications.note: Blog names the Wisconsin Reliability Project and says data centers, utility demand and coal retirements drive Midwest gas investment; names Microsoft and Meta targeting Wisconsin and Illinois.

records.researcher_notes: A Rextag blog from January 2026 names data centers among the demand drivers for the Wisconsin Reliability Project. The project's own fact sheet and the energy agency table name utilities and coal-to-gas conversions only. The data center mention is regional and from a trade blog.

values.DataCenterNotes: A Williams blog post from August 2024 says the Southeast Supply Enhancement project is designed to provide reliable power where data center growth is expected, and points to Virginia as the largest data center hub. The federal regulator's certificate order in 2026 noted that Transco's market study cited data centers among the new large loads. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Williams blog: SSE is designed to provide reliable power where data center growth is expected; Virginia is the largest data center hub.
Reports that the federal regulator accepted a Transco market study citing data center load growth for the project.

records.researcher_notes: Williams's August 2024 blog says the project is designed to supply power where data center growth is expected. A February 2026 law firm summary of the federal regulator's approval says Transco's market study cited data centers and manufacturing as large loads, and the regulator rejected a rival report that called data center demand speculative. No named campus.

values.DataCenterNotes: A January 2025 trade report on Kinder Morgan's Trident pipeline says the project is part of the growing AI data center trend in Texas, citing the chief executive's remarks in the fourth quarter 2024 earnings release. The pipeline's named contracts are for LNG and the Port Arthur industrial corridor. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Article reports Trident as part of the AI data center trend in Texas per CEO Kim Dang's Q4 2024 release remarks.

records.researcher_notes: An Underground Infrastructure article from January 2025 reports that Kinder Morgan's chief executive tied Trident to Texas data center growth. The company's own project page names LNG and industrial demand only, so this is a weaker tie from press reporting of an earnings release.

values.DataCenterNotes: A January 2026 release from Intensity Infrastructure Partners and Rainbow Energy Center says the decision to advance Phase I of the 36-inch pipeline supports sustained data center growth, grid reliability and industrial development in North Dakota. Uncommitted capacity supports new gas-fired power along the route and at Coal Creek Station. No specific data center is named.

verifications.note: Release on advancing Phase I says the project supports sustained data center growth in North Dakota.

records.researcher_notes: The developers' January 2026 release on advancing Phase I names data center growth among the reasons for the project. No campus or customer is named.
